title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #220 ($500)**

For reduced residues a₁ < ⋯ < a_{φ(n)} mod n, is ∑(a_{k+1}-a_k)² ≪ n²/φ(n)?

**Status:** SOLVED (Montgomery-Vaughan 1986)
mathContext: Reduced residues are integers coprime to n. The problem asks if squared gaps are well-controlled.

title: Reduced Residues
mathContext: These form a group under multiplication mod n.

title: Cardinality Equals φ(n)
content:
**card_reducedResidues:**

|reducedResidues n| = φ(n)

This is essentially the definition of Euler's totient function.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of cardinality equals φ(n)

title: Sorted Residues
content:
**sortedResidues n, a n k:**

The reduced residues sorted in increasing order, and the k-th element.

Written as a₁ < a₂ < ⋯ < a_{φ(n)}.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of sorted residues

title: Gap Definition
content:
**gap n k:**

a_{k+1} - a_k

The difference between consecutive reduced residues.
mathContext: Average gap is n/φ(n), but individual gaps can vary significantly.

title: Gap List
content:
**gapList n:**

The list of all gaps [gap(0), gap(1), ..., gap(φ(n)-2)].

There are φ(n) - 1 gaps between φ(n) elements.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of gap list

title: Sum of Gap Powers
content:
**sumGapPowers n γ:**

∑_{k=1}^{φ(n)-1} (a_{k+1} - a_k)^γ

The sum of γ-th powers of all gaps.

**sumSquaredGaps n** is the γ = 2 case.
mathContext: The squared case (γ=2) was Erdős's original question.

title: The Bound n²/φ(n)
content:
**boundedSquaredGaps n:**

n² / φ(n)

This is the "expected" squared sum if all gaps were equal to average n/φ(n).
mathContext: φ(n) gaps of size (n/φ(n)) each gives sum = φ(n) · (n/φ(n))² = n²/φ(n).

title: Erdős Conjecture
content:
**erdos_220_conjecture:**

∃C > 0: ∀n ≥ 1, ∑(gap)² ≤ C · n²/φ(n)

The squared gaps sum is at most a constant times the "all-equal" bound.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of erdős conjecture

title: General γ-Power Bound
mathContext: Erdős posed this general version in 1973.

title: Montgomery-Vaughan (Squares)
content:
**montgomery_vaughan_squared:**

∃C > 0: ∀n ≥ 1, ∑(gap)² ≤ C · n²/φ(n)

The main result confirming Erdős's conjecture.

title: Montgomery-Vaughan (General)
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of montgomery-vaughan (general)

title: Average Gap
content:
**averageGap n:**

n / φ(n)

With φ(n) residues spread over [1,n-1], average spacing is n/φ(n).
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of average gap

title: Prime Case
content:
**prime_case:**

For prime p, reduced residues are {1, 2, ..., p-1} with all gaps = 1.

Sum of squares = p - 2, bound = p²/(p-1) ≈ p. Bound holds easily.
mathContext: Primes give the simplest case where all gaps are equal.

title: Power of 2 Case
content:
**power_of_two_case:**

For n = 2^k, residues are {1, 3, 5, ..., 2^k - 1} with all gaps = 2.

Sum = 2^{k+1}, bound = 2^{k+1}. The bound is TIGHT here.
mathContext: Powers of 2 show the bound is essentially optimal.

title: Jacobsthal's Function
content:
**jacobsthal n:**

max{gap} = maximum gap between consecutive reduced residues.

Related to the smallest prime not dividing n.
mathContext: Large gaps can occur but are rare enough not to dominate the sum.

title: Maximum Gap Bound
content:
**maximum_gap_bound:**

max(gap) ≤ C · (n/φ(n)) · (log n)²

The maximum gap is at most average times a logarithmic factor.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of maximum gap bound

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_220_summary:**

Combines all components: Montgomery-Vaughan proved the squared gaps conjecture.

∑(gap)² ≪ n²/φ(n)
mathContext: The theorem statement captures the complete resolution.

title: Problem Solved
content:
**erdos_220_solved:**

Erdős Problem #220 was completely resolved by Montgomery-Vaughan (1986).

The $500 prize problem is solved.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of problem solved
